elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.6 requires only insurance "including product liability insurance ... consistent with normal business practices" with no monetary limits; the inserted Minimum Coverages paragraph addresses only E&O and cyber. No per-occurrence CGL figure appears anywhere.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL limit is stated in retained 14.6 or in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets E&O at "not less than USD 1,000,000", which is the fallback floor, not the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets cyber and privacy liability at "not less than USD 2,000,000", below the preferred USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Neither 14.6 nor the inserted paragraph mentions workers' compensation or statutory employer coverage.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.6: "Each Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such insurance upon request", which delivers evidence/certificates on request from RevMed.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "RevMed shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000" — counterparty-directed, exact fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "... and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" — counterparty-directed, exact fallback floor.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies both required floors (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000) and imposes them on RevMed, the counterparty, in operative language rather than in the comment.

The preferred level fails on four elements — no CGL per-occurrence or aggregate limits, E&O set at 1M rather than 2M, cyber set at 2M rather than 5M, and no workers' compensation obligation. To reach preferred the drafter would have to state CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2,000,000, raise cyber/privacy to USD 5,000,000, and add statutory workers' compensation.
Certificates-on-request is already satisfied by retained 14.6 ("evidence of such insurance upon request"), so no edit was needed there; the drafter correctly left it alone.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no words outside the two chosen elements are touched, and the insertion omits model-language extras (no at-own-expense wording, no one-year survival tail, no certificate or notice procedure duplicating the retained evidence-on-request and cancellation-notice mechanics).

Intent is preserved: Sanofi's self-insurance right, the mutual product-liability obligation, the cancellation/non-renewal notice from RevMed, and the express statement that insurance does not cap Article XIV indemnity liability all survive without contradiction; the added minimums sit alongside, not against, the "consistent with normal business practices" standard.

Minor drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): the inserted paragraph is untitled by section number and its coverages are arguably outside the antecedent "such insurance" in 14.6's evidence and cancellation-notice sentences; folding the two limits into 14.6 itself, or adding "such insurance shall include", would remove any doubt that the evidence-on-request mechanic reaches the new coverages.
Severity stays low: the agreement already contains a mutual insurance obligation with evidence-on-request, so the gap is limited to unspecified monetary floors.
